messages:
jess (support): FYI customer ACME hit a 400 on /v1/rerank with 'dimension_mismatch' when sending batched embeddings. Request ID req_01A2B3C. They say it only happens on ~10% of batches :/
ryan (eng-ml): Can you paste the exact curl + minimal payload they used and the server error log for req_01A2B3C?
jess (support): Sure — customer provided this curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-rerank-1",
    "queries": ["Which product is cheapest?"],
    "candidates": [["prodA","prodB"]],
    "embeddings": [
      [[0.12, 0.03, ... 0.25], [0.11, 0.02, ... 0.24]]  // they send batched embeddings here
    ]
  }'
```
jess (support): Server responded with 400 and body: `{"error":"dimension_mismatch","expected":1536,"got":1535,"request_id":"req_01A2B3C"}`
ryan (eng-ml): Interesting — expected 1536 (our model) but got 1535. Could be client-side truncation/serialization issue or an off-by-one in their batching code. Ask them to dump JSON lengths and sha256 of payload.
maria (sre): Also please collect the service logs for req_01A2B3C and the proxy logs. I can grab them if you give me the time window (approx ts 1769201220-1769201260).
sara (support): I've asked the customer to run a minimal repro script and return the exact bytes. I included a tiny Python snippet to reproduce locally:
```
import json, requests
p = {
  "model": "redwood-rerank-1",
  "queries": ["Which product is cheapest?"],
  "candidates": [["prodA","prodB"]],
  "embeddings": [[[0.0]*1536, [0.0]*1536]]
}
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', json=p, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REPRO_TOKEN'})
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```
sara (support): I told them to compare length of json.dumps(p).encode() and sha256 to what they send in prod.
jess (support): Customer replied — they ran it and the python repro returns 200 fine. But when they send from their Go service that constructs embeddings with `make([]float32, dim)` then encodes to JSON they sometimes drop the last element (due to a bug in their custom marshaller). Repro case attached with request id req_01A2B3C and sample payload hex.
ryan (eng-ml): If it's intermittent and tied to their marshaller that's likely client-side. Two asks: 1) can they send the raw bytes/hex of the failing payload (we need the exact JSON bytes), 2) we should improve server error message to include an example index so they don't have to binary-search. I'll file a small fix.
maria (sre): Collected server logs for the req window — I see the validate_embeddings() hook rejecting after parsing. Log snippet:
```
2026-03-12T15:07:43.512Z validate_embeddings: req=req_01A2B3C expected_dim=1536 got_dim=1535 path=/v1/rerank client_ip=34.78.12.9
```
jess (support): Customer also mentioned a billing spike because they retried same batch 8x. Billing ticket bill_7f4a opened, told them we've refunded retries while we investigate.
sara (support): Customer sent the raw hex and we confirmed last byte `...f3` missing one float value in the last vector — matches 1535. Sent them a quick checklist: use official SDK, ensure marshaller preserves trailing zeros, or include explicit `vector_dim` field as a guard.
ryan (eng-ml): I'll push a tiny server-side improvement: return field `error_context: { "candidate_index": N }` where N is the vector index closest to the length mismatch, plus link to debug bundle. Should help future triage.
deploy-bot: staging deploy of 2026-03-12/validate-emb-dim-fix succeeded (sha: abc123) :white_check_mark:
jess (support): Customer confirmed workaround (switching to stdlib JSON encoder) fixed the problem. They will run load tomorrow and report back.
ryan (eng-ml): Follow-up actions: (1) add clearer error message + example index (deployed to staging), (2) add small note in support KB about embedding payload validation and common client pitfalls, (3) consider adding a nibble-length field in API to tolerate trailing precision errors? open to opinions.
maria (sre): Marking logs retained under req_01A2B3C in case they reproduce.
sara (support): Closing ticket once customer verifies load test. Thanks team :thumbsup:
